description: List orders (material and item requests) in the organization, newest first, grouped by active vs closed. Order managers see all orders; other members see only orders they requested or are assigned to (`isManager` says which view this is). Each row: id, status, requester, deliver-to target, the free-text request, the requested lines (a specific item, any instance of a model (`modelId`), any item of a category (`categoryId`), or free text; each with its `quantity` where one was given: "5 Packungen Kopierpapier" is quantity 5), `neededByAt` (when the requester needs it; absent when not given), the assignee and `webUrl`, the order's page in the web app. Every date comes twice, the epoch and its ISO twin: `neededByAtIso` is a plain calendar day ("2026-08-11"), `createdAtIso` / `closedAtIso` are UTC instants; the server does no timezone conversion. Statuses: "open" = requested, nobody has started fulfilling it; "in_fulfillment" = an order manager is working on it; "fulfilled" (delivered), "rejected" (declined by a manager) and "cancelled" (withdrawn by the requester) are closed. "Open orders" in the everyday sense are open + in_fulfillment. `status` filters the reads themselves, so it reaches older orders of that status rather than narrowing a capped page. Caps: the newest 100 per active status (open, in_fulfillment) and the newest 50 per closed status (fulfilled, rejected, cancelled), with the closed rows then cut to 50 in total; `truncated: true` means the organization has more orders than returned. An order has no printed code; its `id` is the handle for order tool calls.

status.description: Only orders with this status (absent = all)

name: list_orders

isManager.description: False: the rows are only the orders the connected user requested or is assigned to

closedAtIso.description: When the order was closed, ISO-8601 UTC timestamp

createdAtIso.description: When the order was placed, ISO-8601 UTC timestamp

neededByAt.description: When the requester needs it, epoch milliseconds at UTC midnight. Absent when they did not say

neededByAtIso.description: The needed-by date as a plain calendar day, "YYYY-MM-DD". A DAY, not a moment: the server does no timezone conversion

requestedItems.description: Requested lines: an item, a model (any instance), a category (any item in it) or free text

categoryId.description: Category line: any item of this category, subcategories included — the store picks which

modelId.description: Model line: any instance of this model — the store picks which

name.description: Name of the requested item, model or category as it was when ordered

quantity.description: How many were asked for on that line ("5 Packungen Kopierpapier" = 5). Absent when the requester named no amount — on BOTH item and free-text lines

webUrl.description: Link to the order in the web app, for a person to open; `id` is the handle for tool calls

truncated.description: A bounded read hit its cap

title: List orders
